lessons.title: Statement or question?
lessons.goal: Turn a statement into a yes/no question with your voice alone, and let wh-questions fall.

tip.title: The melody does the work
tip.body: Spanish often uses the same words for a statement and a yes/no question: "Tienes frío" (you're cold) and "¿Tienes frío?" (are you cold?). The only difference is the melody, which writing shows with ¿…?. In a statement the voice falls at the end. In a yes/no question it rises from the last stressed syllable: "¿Tienes FRÍ-o↗?". Questions with qué, dónde, cuándo, cómo or quién usually start high on the question word and fall at the end, like statements. A rise on a wh-question sounds softer and friendlier, or means you didn't catch something: "¿Cómo↗?" (Sorry?).

b.n: Does she speak English? / Do you speak English?

stress.note: Yes/no question: the voice rises from frí- to the end.
Statement: the voice falls after ma-ÑA-na.
Wh-question: start high on qué, then fall.

prompts.n: Ask a friend if they're cold.

lessons.title: Exclamations and rhythm
lessons.goal: Sound surprised, enthusiastic or polite, and give every syllable its time.

tip.title: Even syllables, big melody
tip.body: Exclamations with qué or cuánto start high and fall steeply: "¡Qué día!" (what a day!). The same words with a question melody ask something: "¿Qué día?" (what day?). Surprise is a big rise, often on one word: "¿Mañana?" For politeness, soften with a gentle rise and por favor rather than a flat command. Spanish rhythm is syllable-timed: each syllable takes roughly the same time, stressed or not. English squashes unstressed syllables ("choc'late", "int'resting"); Spanish doesn't. Say ne-ce-si-to with four clear syllables and full vowels, and don't swallow little words like me, de, un, por.

stress.note: Start high on qué and fall.

stress.t: Me gustaría un café, por favor.
stress.mark: Me gusta*rí*a un ca*fé*, por fa*vor*.
stress.note: Give me, un and por their full time; don't swallow them.

stress.n: I need to study a lot.
stress.note: Syllable-timed: ne-ce-si-to-es-tu-diar-mu-cho, each syllable about the same length.
